lesson_title: One Strip of Card Beats the Wind
hook_text: Four strips make a square that falls flat. Add one strip and nothing can push it over. Then try to twist it.
clip_script: Pin four card strips into a square. Push the top and it folds flat without a fight; it is a mechanism, not a structure. Pin one strip corner to corner. Push again. Solid. The square is now two triangles, and a triangle cannot change shape without a side changing length. Push one way and the diagonal is pulled, tension, and card loves that. Push the other way and it is squashed, compression, and the thin strip bows. So add a second diagonal, an X: whichever way you push, one is pulled and holds. Swap the card for string and it still works, because a pulled string is a perfect tie. Now build a cube from four braced squares and twist it. It twists. Braced faces, free inside. One diagonal through the middle and it locks. Brace every direction, slope the legs inward, put most of your triangles at the bottom where the wind bends hardest. That is a tower.
visual_style: Whiteboard square collapsing then locked by a diagonal; arrows marking tension and compression; a cube twisting until an internal diagonal appears.
mood: Hands-on and triumphant, each push answered by one well-placed strip.
pacing: Push, fold, pin, push, hold; quick tension-compression swap; the twist surprise and its fix.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the pinned square and cube with card and split pins.
